top_choice_rationale: The magic-wavelength optical lattice clock is a distinct principle from the 2005 comb and 2012 single-ion prizes: it cancels the light shift while trapping thousands of atoms. It is mature, reproduced and compared across independent laboratories at the 10^-18 level, and checkable by nature through millimetre-scale gravitational redshift and bounds on varying constants and dark matter. The Katori and Ye allocation matches the identifiable decisive steps (proposal and first realisation, then the route to record systematic control). The citation should name the lattice scheme, not clocks or precision in general. A prize this year is better than none, though the omitted groups and unverified priority record are a real caveat.
recusal_note: none apparent from profile; my own field is superconducting circuits, not metrology, and no tie to Katori or Ye is documented
